The removal of the `eee-broken-1000t` quirk in `meson8b-odroidc1.dts` is a direct consequence of this fix, indicating that the underlying issue causing the need for this quirk has been resolved. Thus, the changes collectively enhance the stability and performance of the Ethernet connection on the affected hardware.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by an incorrectly defined IRQ trigger type for the GMAC IRQ, which was set to `EDGE_RISING` instead of the required `LEVEL_HIGH`. This misconfiguration led to the IRQ not being triggered, resulting in a significant drop in connection speed and network instability.
        
        Commit message:
        arm: dts: meson: Fix IRQ trigger type for macirq

A long running stress test on a custom board shipping an AXG SoCs and a
Realtek RTL8211F PHY revealed that after a few hours the connection
speed would drop drastically, from ~1000Mbps to ~3Mbps. At the same time
the 'macirq' (eth0) IRQ would stop being triggered at all and as
consequence the GMAC IRQs never ACKed.

After a painful investigation the problem seemed to be due to a wrong
defined IRQ type for the GMAC IRQ that should be LEVEL_HIGH instead of
EDGE_RISING.

The change in the macirq IRQ type also solved another long standing
issue affecting this SoC/PHY where EEE was causing the network
connection to die after stressing it with iperf3 (even though much
sooner). It's now possible to remove the 'eee-broken-1000t' quirk as
well.

Fixes: 9c15795a4f96 ("ARM: dts: meson8b-odroidc1: ethernet support")
Signed-off-by: Carlo Caione <ccaione@baylibre.com>
Reviewed-by: Martin Blumenstingl <martin.blumenstingl@googlemail.com>
Tested-by: Martin Blumenstingl <martin.blumenstingl@googlemail.com>
Signed-off-by: Kevin Hilman <khilman@baylibre.com>

        diff --git a/arch/arm/boot/dts/meson.dtsi b/arch/arm/boot/dts/meson.dtsi
index e4645f612712..2ab74860d962 100644
--- a/arch/arm/boot/dts/meson.dtsi
+++ b/arch/arm/boot/dts/meson.dtsi
@@ -274,7 +274,7 @@ ethmac: ethernet@c9410000 {
 			compatible = "amlogic,meson6-dwmac", "snps,dwmac";
 			reg = <0xc9410000 0x10000
 			       0xc1108108 0x4>;
-			interrupts = <GIC_SPI 8 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING>;
+			interrupts = <GIC_SPI 8 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
 			interrupt-names = "macirq";
 			status = "disabled";
 		};

Here is the commit message:
arm: dts: meson: Fix IRQ trigger type for macirq

A long running stress test on a custom board shipping an AXG SoCs and a
Realtek RTL8211F PHY revealed that after a few hours the connection
speed would drop drastically, from ~1000Mbps to ~3Mbps. At the same time
the 'macirq' (eth0) IRQ would stop being triggered at all and as
consequence the GMAC IRQs never ACKed.

After a painful investigation the problem seemed to be due to a wrong
defined IRQ type for the GMAC IRQ that should be LEVEL_HIGH instead of
EDGE_RISING.

The change in the macirq IRQ type also solved another long standing
issue affecting this SoC/PHY where EEE was causing the network
connection to die after stressing it with iperf3 (even though much
sooner). It's now possible to remove the 'eee-broken-1000t' quirk as
well.

Fixes: 9c15795a4f96 ("ARM: dts: meson8b-odroidc1: ethernet support")
Signed-off-by: Carlo Caione <ccaione@baylibre.com>
Reviewed-by: Martin Blumenstingl <martin.blumenstingl@googlemail.com>
Tested-by: Martin Blumenstingl <martin.blumenstingl@googlemail.com>
Signed-off-by: Kevin Hilman <khilman@baylibre.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrectly defined IRQ trigger type for the GMAC IRQ, which was set to `EDGE_RISING` instead of the required `LEVEL_HIGH`. This misconfiguration led to the IRQ not being triggered, resulting in a significant drop in connection speed and network instability.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
interrupts = <GIC_SPI 8 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING>;
```
Reason:
The IRQ trigger type for the GMAC IRQ was incorrectly set to `EDGE_RISING`, which means the IRQ would only be triggered on a rising edge of the signal. This configuration caused the IRQ to not be triggered consistently, leading to the IRQ not being acknowledged and resulting in a drastic drop in connection speed and network instability.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
interrupts = <GIC_SPI 8 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
```
Reason:
Changing the IRQ trigger type to `LEVEL_HIGH` ensures that the IRQ remains active as long as the signal is high, allowing for consistent triggering of the IRQ. This fix resolves the issue of the IRQ not being triggered, thereby stabilizing the network connection and preventing the drop in speed.
